title: Burst coverage rotations & price-sensitivity scratchbook
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working spreadsheet-style note to sketch a short-term headcount plan to support increased burst coverage (night/weekend + surge rotation) and to quickly estimate how small changes to hosted API pricing could change demand and hence run-rate capacity needs. Not final — this is intentionally lightweight and noisy.

High-level ask:
- Cover current product reliability gaps during peak hours (US-east evenings, APAC mornings) without committing to large reserved capacity.
- Build a minimal rotation/hiring plan that can be dialed up or down with pricing nudges.
- Produce quick sensitivity pivots for pricing +/- 5/10/20% and show implied marginal FTE need given assumed elasticity.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline MRR (hosted API token revenue) = $2.2M ARR => ~183k ARR/month (for quick calc use $183k).
- Current baseline sustained GPU usage covered by existing staff and reserved capacity; burst windows add ~22% incremental token volume during ~8 hours/day across timezones.
- Average fully-loaded cost per new SRE/Infra-support FTE = $200k/year => $16.7k/month. For rotational hires expect 15% premium (overtime/shift differential) => $19.2k/month effective.
- Elasticity: crude demand elasticity of -0.6 (5% price up => -3% demand). We will test -0.3 to -1.0 range.
- Marginal capacity scaling: each new FTE can reliably manage ~30% more burst-concurrency capacity relative to current (due to automation and on-call). For rough mapping: 1 FTE ~= 120 GPU-hours/week of practical surge ops coverage.

Simplified scenario table (calc notes inline):
Columns: scenario | price delta | demand delta (elasticity -0.6) | delta tokens/month | implied GPU-hour delta | implied incremental FTEs (round up) | incremental monthly cost
1) status-quo | 0% | 0% | 0 | 0 | 0 | $0
2) price +5% | +5% | -3% | -0.03 * baseline_tokens (~-120M tokens) => lowers burst need | - approx -360 GPU-hrs/mo | -1 FTE saved (defer hire) | -$19,200/mo avoided
3) price -5% | -5% | +3% | + approx +120M tokens | +360 GPU-hrs/mo | +1 FTE needed | +$19,200/mo
4) price -10% | -10% | +6% | +240M tokens | +720 GPU-hrs/mo | +2 FTEs | +$38,400/mo
5) price -20% | -20% | +12% | +480M tokens | +1,440 GPU-hrs/mo | +4 FTEs | +$76,800/mo

Notes on numbers: baseline_tokens is a shorthand: using observed monthly token throughput (approx 4B tokens baseline) -> 3% = 120M. GPU-hour mapping is engineering estimate pulled from SRE runbook v2.0. The FTE mapping is conservative (allow for automation gains).

Coverage rotation headcount sketch (shift model):
- Plan A (Lean, fast): 2 x rotational SREs (weekend/nights), 1 x swing (on-call float) => 3 FTE additions. Rationale: quick coverage for peak windows and one dedicated person for incident triage.
- Plan B (Scale): 4 x rotational SREs, 2 x swing => 6 FTE additions. Rationale: expected if price is cut aggressively or new enterprise customers drive sustained peaks.
- Plan C (Auto-heavy): 1 x rotational SRE + automation contractor (3 months) => 1 FTE + 1 contractor. Rationale: short runway where automation reduces ops load quickly.

Quick spreadsheet snapshot (monthly run-rate delta):
- Plan A incremental cost: 3 * $19.2k = $57.6k/month (FTEs) + one-time onboarding tools cost ~$12k -> first month ~69.6k then 57.6k/mo ongoing.
- Plan B incremental cost: 6 * $19.2k = $115.2k/month + onboarding ~$18k.
- Plan C incremental cost: 1 * $19.2k = $19.2k/mo + contractor 3m @$12k/mo = +$36k for first 3 months -> month1 ~55.2k then 19.2k/mo after contractor ends (assuming automation sticks).

Breakeven pricing delta thought-experiment:
- If Plan A results in enabling 10% more tokens/month (net revenue up), using baseline revenue mapping: 10% ARR uplift = ~$18.3k/month gross. That does NOT cover Plan A incremental cost. So to justify Plan A purely via price/demand, you'd need to either raise price or capture higher-margin enterprise mix.
- Conversely, a small price increase (+5%) reduces demand enough to potentially delay Plan A for 2-3 months (depending on observed run-rate).

Operational risks / unknowns (to resolve):
- True marginal GPU-hour per token varies by model mix (gpt-like vs embed heavy flows). Need product to break out token mix for the last 90 days (CONFLUENCE-5721 -> request).
- On-call fatigue and retention risk with rotational premium only; consider contractor bench or overtime budget.
- Customer SLA/contract language: enterprise customers with strict p99 latency might push us to Plan B regardless of price sensitivity. Link to sales signals: JIRA-FIN-214 (enterprise peak tickets).

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Get 90-day token by model split export from billing pipeline (ask billing-eng, ticket created).
- [ ] Run a short A/B price test for low-volume segment (5% up test) to validate elasticity estimate. Owner: Zara.
- [ ] Model weekend-only incremental incidents for the last 6 months to see if 2 rotational hires cover 80% of incidents. Owner: Liam.
- [ ] Confirm recruiting lead time (time-to-hire) for SRE rotational is ~8 weeks; if >10 weeks, prefer contractor bridge. Owner: People Ops (Ethan to coordinate).

Proposed immediate action (next 2 weeks):
1) Lock Plan C as a safety: approve budget for 1 FTE + 3m contractor ($55–60k runway) — quick win and small commitment.
2) Start pricing A/B test for a narrow product slice (5% up; 2-week run). If demand drop <2% then cancel Plan C; if drop >4% keep Plan C and iterate pricing.
3) Build a simple dashboard in Console: burst token volume by local hour + incident count overlay (owner: observability team).

Slack refs / context threads:
- #finance: "need surge ops plan" (starts 2026-05-07)
- #sre-ops: "night-ops coverage gaps" (ticketed 2026-04-30)

Version notes (this doc):
- 2026-05-14 initial sketch (Priya)
- 2026-05-21 added elasticity scenarios + Plan A/B/C cost snapshots (Liam/Zara)
- 2026-06-02 updated numbers with recruitment lead-time; flagged immediate Plan C ask (Ethan)

Rough decision checklist for exec review:
- Required monthly burn for Plan C: ~55–60k for first 3 months (approve from contingency).
- Trigger to move to Plan A: sustained burst windows >20% of weekday traffic for 4 consecutive weeks despite price nudge.
- Trigger to move to Plan B: major enterprise contract signed with 99.99% SLA or expected sustained tokens >+10% for 8 weeks.

Notes-to-self (choppy):
- keep this doc terse; convert to full sheet if exec wants numbers broken into per-role rows.
- want a one-pager for CFO with 3 lines: cost, justification, trigger.
